text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--- The number of new companies in Denmark is the lowest in Europe which has now made the Danish Chamber of Commerce criticise Danish policy on start-up subsidies.
--- 40 young demonstrators were arrested in Sunday for occupying an artificial island, part of the fixed bridge and tunnel link, between Denmark and Sweden as a protest against the project.

--- With a couple of years' delay the Danish building boom has finally reached Copenhagen and unemployment among building workers in the capital is now down to 6.9 percent compared to last year's 8.5 percent.

--- New figures from Denmark's central bank show that Danes are now ready to borrow money for consumer durable goods again, encouraged by increasing employment and higher wages. The figures show thatDanes took out six percent more loans in June this year compared to June 1995.

--- The Danish tourist industry is to spend 5-6 million crowns on getting more business tourists to the country for meetings and conferences. Industry planners hope for an extra turnover of 300 million crowns within the next couple of years.

--- Denmark fails to obtain thousands of jobs as Danish development aid does not involve Danish firms enough in its projects. If Danish firms were to obtain additional orders worth one billion crowns it would mean 1400 new jobs and 500 million crowns more in state revenue.
--- The growing market for mail order companies in Denmark has made large foreign mail order companies aim at Denmark as a country for new growth potential.

--- Education Minister, Ole Vig Jensen, says he will not support a proposal from the Social Democrats to let local authorities decide whether to continue offering mother-tongue teaching in their schools for second generation immigrants.
